title: Lift a long thin panel at points that keep it flat
instruction: Carry the long blue circuit-board panel to the orange rack with both arms, set it down on the rack's rail and let go of it.
context: Industrial electronics manufacturing: production workers who move PCB panels (51-9199) must keep a long thin panel inside its flatness limit on the way to the rack. 4 mm of bow over a 60 cm panel is 0.67 %, inside the 0.75 % bow and twist limit for surface-mount boards. Lifted by its two ends, this 0.8 mm FR-4 panel's middle sags well past that, and held near its middle both ends droop. Held about a fifth of its length in from each end, it stays flat. The instruction names no hold points: the robot must pick where to hold a bending part, which a rigid pick and place never asks.
setup: Positions are centres in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Bench rail: a black aluminium bar 3.6 x 64 x 1.2 cm (64 cm along y) centred at (26, 0), its top 3 cm above the table, on three 2 x 2 cm dark steel legs at y = -28, 0 and 28, fixed. Panel: a blue FR-4 circuit-board panel 60 x 6 cm and 0.8 mm thick (60 cm along y), 18 um copper on both faces over about 40 % of each, six 10 cm boards in one piece (printed lines between them, not cut), populated on its top face only with a QFP, SMD parts, two electrolytic capacitors, a screw terminal and a pin header per board, 120 g +- 3 g in all (53 g bare), bending stiffness EI = 0.07 N m2 +- 10 % (a 20 g weight lowers a 25 cm overhang by 14.6 mm), centred at (26, 0) and lying on the bench rail with its lower face on the rail's top. Rack: an orange aluminium bar 3.6 x 64 x 1.2 cm (64 cm along y) centred at (40, 0), its top 8 cm above the table (5 cm above the bench rail), on three 2 x 2 cm dark steel legs at y = -28, 0 and 28, fixed. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Bow: the largest gap between the panel's centreline and the straight line through its points 1.5 cm in from each end. In a real trial a fixed 4K, 60 fps side camera looks along x so the panel is edge-on, calibrated with a checkerboard and a 3.00 mm gauge block, and the bow is read in every frame from the silhouette without touching the panel. In the simulator the scorer takes the centres of the panel's 20 segments at every control step. Peak bow is the largest bow at any frame or step of the trial. 0 if the peak bow goes over 4 mm at any time, if any part of the panel falls more than 2 cm below the table top, or if the whole panel was never lifted clear (every segment at least 3 cm above its start height at the same step). Otherwise 1.0 (success, held 1 s) if at the end the panel lies on the rack's rail, still, and is let go, with a peak bow of 3 mm or less. 'On the rail' means every segment's centre within 2 cm of the rail's line along x and within 1 mm of lying on it (lower face on the rail), and the panel's centre within 2 cm of the rail's middle along y. 'Still' means every segment under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s. 'Let go' means no part of either gripper's fingers within 3 mm of the panel. A panel held still on the rack, with a finger on it, does not score 1.0. 0.75 if it lies still on the rack and let go with a peak bow over 3 mm and up to 4 mm. 0.5 if it was lifted clear with a peak bow of 4 mm or less but does not end still, on the rack and let go (still carried or held, or set down anywhere else, the bench rail included). So 0, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Lay the panel back on the bench rail, centred at x = 26 cm, flat, with its lower face on the rail. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the demo is open loop and the panel is never jittered. A 4 mm bow does not damage the panel, so the same panel can be reused, but weigh it (120 g +- 3 g) and check its stiffness (cantilever test in the README) before the first trial.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The panel is 20 rigid 3 cm segments, 0.8 mm thick like the board, on hinges with springs set to EI = 0.07 N m2, 120 g spread evenly (the real one has six lumps: same bows within 2 %). It bends in one plane only, no twist or sideways bend. Nothing breaks: the 4 mm limit is only scored. Rails are fixed boxes. Pads close at 50 N. Parts and traces are drawn, not modelled.
scores: Dream-1 was not run on this version. Demo: 1.0 (success at step 237)
